_comment: What each machine actually does when Codex tries to sandbox a command.
Every entry here was measured by scripts/diagnose_codex_sandbox_host.py on
the machine it names, and nothing is written here from expectation. A host
with no entry is a host nobody has looked at: the checker treats that as a
failure to be resolved by measuring, never as a pass.
GitHub-hosted entries on every relevant change, and fails when a host stops
matching its record. That is the point of the file. Hosted runner images are
rebuilt continuously, so the day one of them starts running a command under
bubblewrap is the day this project gains an execution host for free -- and
without something watching, nobody would find out.
'ready' is the only value that means a command actually ran inside the
sandbox. Every other value is a named wall; see the docstring of the
diagnostic for what each one means and which of them a person can move.

xenology-nas.os: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS userspace on a Synology DSM kernel
xenology-nas.note: No /proc/sys/user at all -- user namespaces became a sysctl in 4.9, and this kernel is 3.10. Nothing installable or configurable on this box changes the answer, which is why the execution host has to come from somewhere else.
xenology-nas.measured_by: scripts/diagnose_codex_sandbox_host.py, run directly on the box
